stages.choice_rule: Four different whole words from the roots list. Three share one vowel sound. answer_index is the one word with a different vowel sound. Shuffle that word across the four slots. Tier 1 is an easy team, as in boat, tree, or rain. Tier 2 and tier 3 use closer variant vowels.

roots: Four whole words from the roots list. Exactly one has a different vowel sound, and that word is the only answer.
The other three must share one vowel sound in American English. Same spelling is not required, but the sound must match.
Never put two different vowel sounds in the matching trio, and never make two answers possible.
Do not use a word that can be read two ways, such as read, live, close, wind, or tear.
Tier 1 uses an easy vowel team, as in boat, tree, or rain, plus one obvious mismatch such as cat, pig, or hot.
Tier 2 splits a variant vowel, such as book beside moon, snow beside cow, or beach beside bread.
Tier 3 is a near miss with the same vowel letters, such as soup beside house or sweat beside wheat.
Stems must be one of these only: Which word has a different vowel? Tap the word with a different vowel. Now pick the word with a different vowel. <NAME>, pick the word with a different vowel.
Use whole words only. Do not write IPA, slash sounds, letter sounds alone, or a held vowel.
Shuffle the different word across slots. Set explain_key from miss_explain. Do not write new explanation prose.
Two-syllable words are allowed only when the compared vowel is clear and syllable count does not create a second answer.
No brand names and no real child names. Use the NAME swap only in the name stem frame.

tier_rules.1: Short stem and four one-syllable words. Three share an easy vowel, as in boat, coat, and road. The different word is obvious, as in cat, pig, or hot.
tier_rules.2: Grade 2 variant vowels. Three words share a sound, as in moon, boot, and spoon, or cow, town, and down. The different word is close but clear, as in book, snow, or beach.
tier_rules.3: Near misses with the same vowel letters and a different sound, as in soup beside house or sweat beside wheat. Two-syllable words only when one vowel is clearly different.
